segments.narration: Hundreds of skulls in this frozen lake had matching round holes. Deep in the Himalayas, Lake Roopkund hid hundreds of skeletons frozen in ice.
At sixteen thousand feet, no roads existed. For decades, people assumed a lost army perished here.
Then scientists examined the bones. Every single victim was struck by a heavy object directly from above. What hits hundreds of people at once from the sky?
DNA testing and radiocarbon dating revealed the remains are from two separate events dating to around 800 CE and 1800 CE.
Trapped on the bare ridge, an ancient caravan was killed in minutes by giant falling hail.

verdicts.claim: Hundreds of human skeletons with matching round impact fractures were discovered at Lake Roopkund.
verdicts.note: The reference article states hundreds of human skeletons were found with head injuries caused by round objects from above.

verdicts.claim: Lake Roopkund is located at an altitude of sixteen thousand feet in the Himalayas.
verdicts.note: The reference article states Roopkund is a glacial lake in the Himalayas at an altitude of 5,020 m (16,470 ft).

verdicts.claim: Forensic examination showed the Roopkund victims suffered fatal blows to the head coming from directly above.
verdicts.note: The reference article notes that studies of the skeletons revealed head injuries caused by round objects from above as the common cause of death.

verdicts.claim: DNA testing and radiocarbon dating revealed the remains date back to around eight hundred AD.
verdicts.note: DNA testing (genome-wide analysis) combined with radiocarbon dating showed the remains are from two distinct eras (~800 CE and ~1800 CE), rather than dating exclusively to ~800 CE.
verdicts.correction: DNA testing and radiocarbon dating revealed the remains are from two separate events dating to around 800 CE and 1800 CE.

verdicts.claim: Forensic scientists concluded the victims were struck down by giant hail around three inches in diameter.
verdicts.note: The article mentions researchers concluded the victims were caught in a hailstorm with round objects hitting from above, but it does not specify the measurement or diameter of the hail.

verdicts.claim: The Roopkund victims were travelers caught in the open on a high ridge with no shelter from the storm.
verdicts.note: The article mentions a pilgrimage party perishing near the lake in a storm, but does not state they were on a high ridge with no shelter.
